merged.title: xs-wire: the configuration frames that follow HELLO
merged.summary: Added the post-HELLO configuration frames to xs-wire: IO, COMPRESS, XATTR, ACL, CHOWN, SPARSE, LINKDEST, RELATIVE, FILES_CONFIG/DATA/END, FILTER, DELETE, PRUNE and OUTPUT. Encoding matches run_client byte for byte, decoding checks framing, negotiated features and hostile-peer bounds. Unit byte tests and a C++ server interop test pass, along with clippy and fmt.

merged.title: xs-rs MVP: a Linux client and server that copy trees to and from the C++ xs, at least as fast
merged.summary: Added the xs-rs binary crate with a Linux client and server that speak the C++ xs version 4 stream in both directions. A C++ client can push to and pull from xs-rs, and xs-rs can push to and pull from a C++ xs server; trees compare equal including modes, nanosecond mtimes, symlinks, empty entries and non-UTF-8 names, with compressed and no-op transfers verified.

merged.title: zstd: compressed directory listings and data blocks (PF_ZSTD)
merged.summary: Ported the PF_ZSTD compression policy into xs-rs: exact C++ suffix-list parsing, F_COMPRESS_CONFIG negotiation and refusal, compression sampling, adaptive levels, and per-suffix isolation of raw DATA blocks. Rust clients and servers now exchange ZSTD directory listings and data blocks with the C++ xs and refuse hostile or unnegotiated compression frames.

merged.title: user and group names (PF_IDMAP, PF_CHOWN)
merged.summary: Implemented PF_IDMAP name records and PF_CHOWN ownership configuration in xs-rs, matching remote.cpp and ownership.cpp. The C++ client can now push/pull names and --chown overrides to/from xs-rs, and hostile or unnegotiated ownership frames are refused with the reference exit codes.

merged.title: keepalives, bandwidth limits and timeouts (PF_IO_CONTROL)
merged.summary: Implemented PF_IO_CONTROL in xs-rs: exact --bwlimit/--timeout parsing, the token-bucket rate limiter, F_IO_CONFIG negotiation in the C++ order, negotiated keep-alives, and idle-timeout exit code 30. C++ clients and servers interoperate in both directions, and hostile or older peers are refused for invalid or unnegotiated keep-alives and malformed I/O configuration.

merged.title: itemized output and progress (PF_OUTPUT, PF_DIR_OUTPUT, PF_PROGRESS_ACK)
merged.summary: Added the itemized-output and progress-acknowledgment protocol to xs-rs and xs-wire. C++ clients now get itemized events from xs-rs receivers, xs-rs clients render C++ receiver events, DIR frames carry the negotiated output metadata, and progress acknowledgments are bounded and feature-gated. All three gate commands pass with XS_BIN set to the parent C++ xs.

merged.title: hard links (PF_HLINK)
merged.summary: Implemented PF_HLINK in xs-rs: DIR entries and DATA file attributes now carry the C++ hdev/ino/nlink/ctime/ctime_ns fields, -H negotiates the feature, and the receiver groups source inodes, sends each group's data once, links aliases after transfer, and itemizes them exactly as the C++ xs does. Cross-direction C++/Rust push, pull and local copies preserve hard-link topology, including symlink and FIFO aliases.

agent.summary: Split the oversized xs-rs transfer engine into sender/shared, receiver, hard-link and destination-file modules, and moved the post-HELLO configuration reader out of main.rs into config.rs. Also removed duplicate metadata-kind and partial-file setup code. Added the requested 2026-10-20 README changelog; all four gates pass.
agent.diagnosis: The dominant problem was rs/xs-rs/src/transfer.rs at 1,826 lines, mixing the sender, receiver, hard-link grouping, destination file handling and shared frame/event helpers. I read it end to end, traced which helpers both engines use, and cut at function boundaries so no logic changed. transfer.rs is now 735 lines; the receiver is 687, hard links 266 and destination files 170. main.rs fell from 672 to 528 lines after moving 157 lines of configuration-frame handling into config.rs. The measured change is 2,562 lines including the README entry, under the 3,000-line budget.
agent.change: Moved the receiver engine to transfer/receiver.rs, hard-link logic to transfer/hardlink.rs and destination file helpers to transfer/file.rs, leaving the sender and shared helpers in transfer.rs. Extracted read_configuration, config_frame and read_config_frame into src/config.rs. Reused scan::kind_of instead of a duplicate metadata-kind mapping in the hard-link code. Factored the duplicated InFile construction used by DATA CHUNK and END records into open_infile. Removed process_dir's unused input parameter. Added module documentation and the dated README changelog listing all seven merged steps and the four cleanups.
agent.expected_effect: No behaviour or wire-byte changes. The crate is easier to navigate by responsibility, with the sender, receiver, hard-link and file-publishing concerns separated and the configuration protocol isolated from process startup. Duplicated logic is reduced, so future receiver and configuration changes have one place to edit.
agent.risks: The refactor is mechanical and all moved functions retain their original bodies except the two deduplications, the unused-parameter removal and visibility annotations needed by sibling modules. The full interop suite in both directions passed, covering compression, ownership, IO control, output and hard links against the C++ xs.
agent.tests: Ran the required XS_BIN=... cargo test: 92 tests passed (12 xs-rs unit, 5 compression, 5 hardlink, 9 interop, 5 io_control, 12 output, 8 ownership, 28 xs-wire unit, 4 wire interop, 4 wire io_control). Also ran cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, and cargo check --all-targets --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu; all passed.
